provenance: Surfaced while proving al-Saʿdī's readings to be instances of Usul.Schema. Each question names an interpretive commitment, the alternatives, the typed pins that fail if it changes, established answers cited from the pinned Ḥanbalī corpus (by record id or source locator), and analogies (internal ones licensed by a shared schema, illustrative ones non-evidential). LLM-drafted; awaiting human review (Review.tla).

basis: halaqa shared/STUB-CLASSIFICATION.md: usul-k/ is class C, reserved to Sharīʿah authority
ICM-H §17: research agents may classify, compare, identify uncertainty and surface questions
ICM-H §32: analytical preparation never satisfies a SHARIAH-AUTHORITY gate
docs/architecture/deontic-circuits-harness.md: the LLM proposes; only human review admits
this_register_may: name the commitment an encoding makes
list alternatives found in the tradition
cite an established answer from a pinned source, with its relation to the commitment
offer analogies: internal ones licensed by a shared schema (qiyās), illustrative ones marked non-evidential
say which formal pins change if the commitment changes
suggest the usul-k home a ruling would eventually live in
this_register_may_not: adopt an answer or rank the alternatives
treat an analogy as outranking a cited text

process.note: The review applies the project's principles to itself where this cannot deadlock (Usul.Process). Status is computed: referenced if an established answer is cited, else analogized if an internal analogy is offered, else open.

uses_why.8: adoption is a gate (SHARIAH-AUTHORITY), never a status here
uses_why.11: status persists until evidence on file changes it
uses_why.58: internal analogies are qiyās through a shared schema; naqḍ rejects a missing tag

avoids.33: IQ-10 is open on Q33's tie-break; choosing among cited answers by 'best' would wait on its own question

questions.commitment: The operative presumption for a claim is barāʾat al-dhimma (no liability), so the denier is whoever agrees with it and the claimant whoever departs from it.
alternatives: The apparent state (al-ẓāhir) as the presumption, which can place the claimant role on the party asserting freedom from liability.
A presumption fixed per bāb rather than one for all claims.
questions.if_changed: Change the presumption argument of burdenOf in q10_from_presumption; the S6 pin for Q10 fails until the new presumption is stated.

established.note: When the presumption (aṣl) and the apparent state (ẓāhir) conflict: an apparent state that is a sharʿī proof (testimony, report) prevails without dispute; one resting on custom, habit, indications or preponderant belief sometimes yields, sometimes prevails, and sometimes the madhhab is divided. A single presumption covers one of these classes only.

analogies.note: As in Q52, an indication strong enough to displace the presumption moves the burden; IQ-01 asks which presumption is displaced.
actori incumbit probatio: the burden lies on whoever asserts a change from the status quo, which is S6 with the status quo as presumption.

questions.commitment: When sense or custom belies a trustee, the presumption that he returned the thing is displaced entirely, and he must bring evidence.
alternatives: Being belied only weakens the presumption: the oath is still accepted, but with a stronger form or added conditions.
Only sense (ḥiss) displaces it; custom (ʿurf) does not.
questions.if_changed: returnPresumption would need a graded result (a Qawaid.Held with a Grade) instead of a Bool, and burden_after_update (Q52) would decide; the Q26/Q43 pins fail.

established.note: For loss, every trustee's word is accepted, since trust means no liability. For return, trustees fall into three classes; one who took the property for the owner's benefit alone is believed (the madhhab), but a narration through Abū Ṭālib and Ibn Manṣūr holds that a deposit proved by evidence is not discharged by a bare claim of return.
Displacement by custom or indication is the second class of aṣl/ẓāhir conflict, where the madhhab goes both ways.

analogies.note: As for claimant and denier, the trustee's role is derived from whether his claim agrees with the presumption.
A bailee for the bailor's sole benefit is held to a lighter standard than one who benefits himself.

questions.commitment: After a confession, every later plea (a claim of error, a retraction) is inert. This reading is for the rights of persons (ḥuqūq al-ādamiyyīn).
alternatives: In the ḥudūd (rights of God) a retraction is accepted, so retract is not inert there and needs its own plead.
A claim of error is inert but a retraction is not, in some domains.
questions.if_changed: A domain parameter on plead; q55_confession_absorbs then holds only for the persons domain, and a second S5 instance (without retract) is pinned for ḥudūd.

established.note: The judge may invite one who confessed to a ḥadd to retract; al-Intiṣār: prompting the retraction is lawful. So in the ḥudūd a retraction is not inert.
established.excerpt_ar: للحاكم أن يعرض للمقر بحد أن يرجع عن إقراره، وقال في الانتصار: تلقينه الرجوع مشروع

established.note: Retracting the confession drops the ḥadd (the case of Māʿiz: 'why did you not leave him to repent').
established.excerpt_ar: فالحيلة أن يرجع عن إقراره فيسقط عنه الحد

analogies.note: As later doubts are inert on a certain judgement (Q11), later pleas are inert on a confession; both are absorbing states.
An admission against interest binds in civil matters, while a criminal confession may be withdrawn before judgment: the same split as persons/ḥudūd.

questions.commitment: Two owed acts merge when kind and purpose are equal, whatever the occasion that made each owed. 'Purpose' is a label compared for equality.
alternatives: Purpose as intention (niyya): merging needs the performer to intend both, or to intend the higher one.
Merging limited to listed kinds (ṭahāra, ḥudūd of one genus) instead of every kind.
questions.if_changed: Merges gains an intention argument or a kind whitelist; it must stay reflexive for reps_covers, and the S7 pin records whether it is still an equivalence.

established.note: Merging requires two acts of one genus at one time, neither performed as a make-up (qaḍāʾ) nor as a dependent of the other; and in the first type both must be intended, on the well-known view (two impurities: the major ablution suffices if both are intended). The reading ignores time, make-up, dependence and intention.

analogies.note: Concurrent sentences: one term covers several convictions only when ordered so and the offences are of a kind, which adds an intention-like condition to the merge relation.

questions.commitment: Liability for destroying property ignores the destroyer's mental state (Q13), and the validity of a disposition ignores the actor's belief about his entitlement (Q54).
alternatives: Mental state matters for sin and punishment but not for compensation (a two-output reading: liability ignores intent, sin does not).
Belief matters where the actor was misled by the other party.
questions.if_changed: Ignores no longer holds; the S1 pins for Q13 and Q54 fail, which is the intended signal that a coordinate became relevant.

established.note: Whoever destroys another's property believing it his own: if the belief rests on a visible cause from another who erred or admits intent, that other is liable; if on bare ijtihād, there are two views on liability. Belief can move liability between parties.
The causes of liability are three: contract, hand and destruction. Destruction is a cause by the act itself, not by the intent behind it.

analogies.note: Loss liability factors through authorisation, not mental state, as destruction liability does in Q13.
Every consequence computed from an invariant ruling is invariant too; if intent were relevant to sin but not to liability, two outputs would be needed.
Strict liability: liability for the act regardless of fault, with fault relevant to other consequences.

questions.commitment: Harm may be inflicted only if it is none, whatever harm was received. Prescribed retaliation (qiṣāṣ) and prescribed penalties are outside the reading, not exceptions inside it.
alternatives: Retaliation modelled inside Q15 as a derogation with its own conditions (equality, authority of the ruler).
questions.if_changed: mayInflict gains a derogation argument; q15_ignores_received holds only off the derogation.

established.note: 'No harm and no reciprocal harm' is a principle our companions reasoned with in many matters; rulings are either for securing benefits or for repelling harms.
established.excerpt_ar: لا ضرر ولا ضرار ... وقد علل أصحابنا بذلك في مسائل كثيرة

analogies.note: The harm received is ignored as intent is ignored in Q13: both readings declare one coordinate irrelevant.
Self-help is barred and retaliation reserved to the court, so the carve-out sits outside the private rule.

questions.commitment: Whoever pays another's obligation has recourse unless he paid as a gift. The heading in the witness is lost to OCR (reading from the index stub).
alternatives: Recourse only when he paid intending to reclaim it (the condition stated positively, which differs when intention is unknown).
Recourse only with the debtor's permission.
questions.if_changed: recourse gains an intention or permission argument, which becomes a second impediment or a condition in q32_is_gate; q32_never_more_than_paid must still hold.

established.note: Recourse for paying another's due without his permission, in the sounder narration (the madhhab of al-Khiraqī, Abū Bakr, al-Qāḍī and most). Al-Qāḍī requires intending recourse and witnessing it at payment: intending a gift or leaving the intention unspecified gives no recourse. The reading grants recourse when the intention is unspecified.

analogies.note: Intention to reclaim as a condition and gift as an impediment, in the same gate algebra as entitlement and hastening in Q17.
Negotiorum gestio and subrogation: the payer's recourse depends on acting for the debtor without donative intent.

questions.commitment: A measure defined by the law strictly precedes custom: custom decides only where the law is silent, and never overrides a defined measure.
alternatives: Custom also specifies (takhṣīṣ) a general legal term, which is not a fallback but a refinement.
questions.if_changed: Custom as a refinement is an S1/S3 reading (a qualifier), not S2; the Q9 pin would move schema.

established.note: Custom specifies a general term: where customary use has made one sense the real one, the general is restricted to it without dispute (an oath not to eat 'roast' covers roast meat only). Custom then refines a term rather than only filling a gap.

analogies.note: Law over custom has the shape of possible intent over the literal (Q57); the refinement alternative changes the shape for both.
The dalīl over the domain default, the same priority shape.

questions.commitment: Allocation follows the order: the known entitled, then division, then lots. Lots are the last resort.
alternatives: Division and lots ranked differently where division destroys value (e.g. an indivisible object).
questions.if_changed: The order of sources in allocation changes; q25_lot_is_last_resort records when lots apply and fails if the order changes.

established.note: Lots distinguish the entitled when entitlement attaches to an unspecified one among equals, or to recover a specific entitled person lost in confusion; not used for lineage. The reading lacks the equality condition and the lineage exclusion.

analogies.note: Original before substitute, as entitled before division before lots.
Stipulated price before value, the same fallback shape.

questions.commitment: Options are compared on one integer scale (benefit, harm, time, strength of evidence). Ties go to the earliest-listed option. The tie-break is an artefact of the encoding, not of the text.
alternatives: Benefits and harms incommensurable in general (a partial order), so a choice may not exist.
Ties resolved by a second criterion (e.g. precaution) instead of list order.
questions.if_changed: A partial order replaces Int; best becomes a set of maximal options, and Optimal.key_unique no longer holds, which the S8 pins expose.

established.note: One noble act against many lesser: Aḥmad's apparent view prefers multiplicity; other narrations prefer the noble one, or equality. Two dimensions and genuine ties occur, where the reading assumes one scale and breaks ties by list order.
Two conflicting presumptions: act on the stronger; if equal, the question is divided in the madhhab. Ties yield disagreement, not an order of listing.

analogies.note: A scalar ranking versus a Pareto (partial) order: under the second, 'the best' may not exist, and Optimal.key_unique fails.

questions.commitment: Establishment by dependence is transitive: a dependent of a dependent of a proved thing is established.
alternatives: Only one step of dependence (a dependent of a proved principal), not the transitive closure.
questions.if_changed: Established becomes one step of the step relation rather than Closure; q50_follower_established then needs a proved principal.

established.note: The same rule: what is not established independently is established as a dependent (women's testimony to birth establishes lineage). Its examples are one step; transitivity is not addressed.

analogies.note: Voidness propagates transitively along 'built on'; IQ-11 asks whether establishment propagates the same way.
The means of a means of an obligation is obligatory: transitivity is accepted in Q2.

questions.commitment: Proved voidness propagates along 'built on' to every dependent contract, transitively. Rescinding a contract that was not proved void leaves the set of void contracts unchanged.
alternatives: Propagation stops at a dependent acquired in good faith by a third party.
Rescission affects dependents concluded after it, which needs time on the relation.
questions.if_changed: A good-faith or time guard on builtOn; q53_rescission_inert still holds, q53_void_propagates gains a hypothesis.

established.note: Al-Qāḍī and Ibn ʿAqīl: rescission for a defect lifts the contract from now; rescission by an option lifts it from its origin, since the option prevents bindingness altogether. 'Rescission is inert' fits rescission for a defect only.
established.excerpt_ar: الفسخ بالعيب رفع للعقد من حينه، والفسخ بالخيار رفع للعقد من أصله

analogies.note: Establishment and voidness are the same closure with different seeds.
Void ab initio (ex tunc) versus voidable and rescinded (ex nunc).
